questions.title: ConfigMap and Secret as environment
questions.text:
In namespace `dev`:

- create a ConfigMap `app-config` with the key `APP_MODE=production`
- create a Secret `app-secret` with the key `DB_PASS=s3cret`
- create a Pod `app` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that exposes `APP_MODE` from the ConfigMap and `DB_PASS` from the Secret as environment variables with the same names
questions.solution:
kubectl -n dev create configmap app-config --from-literal=APP_MODE=production
    kubectl -n dev create secret generic app-secret --from-literal=DB_PASS=s3cret
    kubectl -n dev run app --image=busybox:1.36 $do -- sleep 3600 > app.yaml
    vim app.yaml

Add `env` to the container:

    env:
    - name: APP_MODE
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef:
          name: app-config
          key: APP_MODE
    - name: DB_PASS
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef:
          name: app-secret
          key: DB_PASS

Then `kubectl apply -f app.yaml` and verify with `kubectl -n dev exec app -- env | grep -E 'APP_MODE|DB_PASS'`.

references.title: Configure a Pod to use a ConfigMap

checks.name: app-config
checks.hint: configmap app-config must hold APP_MODE=production

checks.name: app-secret
checks.hint: secret app-secret must hold DB_PASS=s3cret

checks.name: app
checks.hint: pod app must take APP_MODE from configmap app-config

checks.name: app
checks.hint: pod app must take DB_PASS from secret app-secret

checks.hint: pod app is not running

questions.title: A Job with parallel completions
questions.text:
Create a Job named `pi` in namespace `dev` using image `busybox:1.36` that runs `sh -c "echo 3.14159"`.

The Job must complete **2** times with a parallelism of **2**, and must have `backoffLimit: 4`. Wait until it has completed.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n dev create job pi --image=busybox:1.36 $do -- sh -c "echo 3.14159" > pi.yaml
    vim pi.yaml     # add under spec:  completions: 2, parallelism: 2, backoffLimit: 4
    kubectl apply -f pi.yaml
    kubectl -n dev get job pi -w

`kubectl create job` has no flags for completions or parallelism, so generating YAML and editing is the normal route. `kubectl -n dev logs job/pi` shows the output.

checks.name: pi
checks.hint: job pi needs completions 2, parallelism 2, backoffLimit 4, image busybox:1.36

checks.name: pi
checks.hint: job pi has not completed 2 times yet

questions.title: A CronJob
questions.text:
Create a CronJob named `backup` in namespace `dev` with image `busybox:1.36` running `sh -c "echo backup"` every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`).

Set `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` and keep only `2` successful jobs in history.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n dev create cronjob backup --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="*/5 * * * *" $do -- sh -c "echo backup" > backup.yaml
    vim backup.yaml    # under spec: add concurrencyPolicy: Forbid and successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 2
    kubectl apply -f backup.yaml
    kubectl -n dev get cronjob backup

checks.name: backup
checks.hint: cronjob backup: schedule */5 * * * *, concurrencyPolicy Forbid, successfulJobsHistoryLimit 2, image busybox:1.36

questions.title: StatefulSet with a headless Service
questions.text:
In namespace `media` create:

- a headless Service named `db` (clusterIP `None`) selecting `app=db` on port `6379`
- a StatefulSet named `db` with `2` replicas, image `redis:7.2`, container port `6379`, labels `app=db`, using `serviceName: db`

Both pods (`db-0`, `db-1`) must be running.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: Service
    metadata:
      name: db
      namespace: media
    spec:
      clusterIP: None
      selector:
        app: db
      ports:
      - port: 6379
        targetPort: 6379
    ---
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: StatefulSet
    metadata:
      name: db
      namespace: media
    spec:
      serviceName: db
      replicas: 2
      selector:
        matchLabels:
          app: db
      template:
        metadata:
          labels:
            app: db
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: redis
            image: redis:7.2
            ports:
            - containerPort: 6379

StatefulSets create pods one at a time in order (`db-0`, then `db-1` once `db-0` is Ready); the headless Service gives each pod a stable DNS name like `db-0.db.media.svc.cluster.local`.

checks.name: db
checks.hint: service db must be headless (clusterIP None), select app=db, port 6379

checks.name: db
checks.hint: statefulset db must have 2 replicas, serviceName db, image redis:7.2
db-0 and db-1 are not both running

questions.title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
questions.text: Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler for the Deployment `gateway` in namespace `payments` that keeps between `2` and `6` replicas, targeting `70%` average CPU utilization.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n payments autoscale deployment gateway --min=2 --max=6 --cpu-percent=70
    kubectl -n payments get hpa

This creates an `autoscaling/v2` HPA with a `Resource` metric of type `Utilization`. The TARGETS column shows `<unknown>` until metrics-server has samples for the pods.

checks.name: gateway
checks.hint: hpa gateway must target deployment gateway, min 2, max 6, 70% CPU

questions.title: Rolling update and history
questions.text:
Update the Deployment `catalog` in namespace `media` to image `nginx:1.27` using a rolling update, and wait until it is fully rolled out.

Then write the **number of revisions** shown by `kubectl rollout history` for this Deployment into `/opt/answers/catalog-revisions.txt` on the base host.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n media set image deployment/catalog main=nginx:1.27
    kubectl -n media rollout status deployment catalog
    kubectl -n media rollout history deployment catalog     # REVISION 1 and 2
    echo 2 > /opt/answers/catalog-revisions.txt

Each template change creates a new ReplicaSet and a new revision; `rollout undo` would go back to revision 1.

checks.name: catalog
checks.hint: catalog must run image nginx:1.27

checks.name: catalog
checks.hint: catalog is not fully rolled out
/opt/answers/catalog-revisions.txt must contain the revision count (2)

questions.title: Node affinity
questions.text: The nodes carry a `zone` label (`east` / `west`). Create a Pod `east-pod` in namespace `default` with image `nginx:1.27` that uses **required node affinity** (not a nodeSelector) so it can only run on nodes where `zone` is `east`. It must be running.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: east-pod
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: zone
                operator: In
                values:
                - east
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.27

`kubectl get nodes -L zone` shows which node is east; `kubectl get pod east-pod -o wide` confirms placement.

checks.name: east-pod
checks.hint: east-pod must use requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution node affinity, not nodeSelector

checks.name: east-pod
checks.hint: east-pod is not running on the zone=east node

questions.title: Egress NetworkPolicy
questions.text:
In namespace `dev` the Pod `restricted` (label `role=restricted`) must only be able to open **egress** connections to:

- pods labelled `app=api` in the same namespace on TCP port `80`
- DNS (UDP and TCP port `53`) in namespace `kube-system`

Create a NetworkPolicy named `restrict-egress` in `dev` that enforces this. Test pods: `api` (Deployment, `app=api`) should be reachable, `sink` (`app=other`) must not.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: NetworkPolicy
    metadata:
      name: restrict-egress
      namespace: dev
    spec:
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          role: restricted
      policyTypes:
      - Egress
      egress:
      - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: api
        ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 80
      - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
        ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 53

Without the DNS rule the pod could no longer resolve service names. Verify: `kubectl -n dev exec restricted -- wget -qO- --timeout=2 api` works, `... sink` times out.

checks.name: restrict-egress
checks.hint: restrict-egress must select role=restricted and be an Egress policy
restricted must still reach app=api on port 80
restricted must be blocked from reaching app=other

questions.title: Dynamic volume provisioning
questions.text:
A StorageClass `local-dyn` exists. In namespace `payments` create a PersistentVolumeClaim `data-dyn` requesting `2Gi` with access mode `ReadWriteOnce` using that class, and a Pod `writer` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that mounts the claim at `/data`.

The claim must be Bound and the pod running.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: v1
    kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
    metadata:
      name: data-dyn
      namespace: payments
    spec:
      storageClassName: local-dyn
      accessModes:
      - ReadWriteOnce
      resources:
        requests:
          storage: 2Gi
    ---
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Pod
    metadata:
      name: writer
      namespace: payments
    spec:
      volumes:
      - name: data
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: data-dyn
      containers:
      - name: main
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sleep", "3600"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data

With a dynamic StorageClass nobody creates the PersistentVolume by hand: the provisioner creates a `pvc-<uid>` volume and binds it. `kubectl get pv,pvc -n payments` shows both.

checks.name: data-dyn
checks.hint: pvc data-dyn must request 2Gi ReadWriteOnce from class local-dyn

checks.name: data-dyn
checks.hint: pvc data-dyn is not Bound

checks.name: writer
checks.hint: pod writer must mount data-dyn at /data

checks.name: writer
checks.hint: pod writer is not running

questions.title: Cluster-wide RBAC for a user
questions.text:
Create a ClusterRole `node-viewer` that allows `get`, `list` and `watch` on `nodes`, and a ClusterRoleBinding `node-viewer-dave` that grants it to the user `dave`.

`dave` must not be able to delete nodes.
questions.solution:
kubectl create clusterrole node-viewer --verb=get,list,watch --resource=nodes
    kubectl create clusterrolebinding node-viewer-dave --clusterrole=node-viewer --user=dave
    kubectl auth can-i list nodes --as dave      # yes
    kubectl auth can-i delete nodes --as dave    # no

Nodes are cluster-scoped, so a namespaced Role cannot grant access to them — this needs a ClusterRole and a ClusterRoleBinding.

checks.name: node-viewer
checks.hint: clusterrole node-viewer missing

checks.name: node-viewer-dave
checks.hint: clusterrolebinding node-viewer-dave must bind clusterrole node-viewer to user dave
dave cannot list nodes
dave must not be able to delete nodes

questions.title: Gateway API
questions.text:
A GatewayClass `nginx-gc` exists. In namespace `media` there is a Deployment `media` exposed by Service `media` on port `80`.

Create a Gateway named `main-gw` in `media` using that class with one HTTP listener named `http` on port `80`, and an HTTPRoute named `media-route` in `media` attached to `main-gw` that routes host `media.example.com` to Service `media` port `80`.
questions.solution:
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: Gateway
    metadata:
      name: main-gw
      namespace: media
    spec:
      gatewayClassName: nginx-gc
      listeners:
      - name: http
        protocol: HTTP
        port: 80
    ---
    apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
    kind: HTTPRoute
    metadata:
      name: media-route
      namespace: media
    spec:
      parentRefs:
      - name: main-gw
      hostnames:
      - media.example.com
      rules:
      - backendRefs:
        - name: media
          port: 80

Gateway API splits what Ingress bundled: the GatewayClass is the implementation, the Gateway is the listener, and HTTPRoutes attach to it via `parentRefs`.

checks.name: main-gw
checks.hint: gateway main-gw must use class nginx-gc with an HTTP listener 'http' on port 80

checks.name: media-route
checks.hint: httproute media-route must attach to main-gw, match media.example.com, and route to service media:80

questions.title: Extract a value with jsonpath
questions.text: Using `kubectl` with a **jsonpath** output, write the InternalIP address of node `cka2-node1` into `/opt/answers/node1-ip.txt` on the base host (the address only, nothing else).
questions.solution:
kubectl get node cka2-node1 -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}' > /opt/answers/node1-ip.txt
    cat /opt/answers/node1-ip.txt

The `[?(@.type=="InternalIP")]` filter picks the matching entry from the addresses list. Explore the structure first with `kubectl get node cka2-node1 -o yaml`.

checks.hint: /opt/answers/node1-ip.txt must contain exactly the InternalIP of cka2-node1

questions.title: Decode a Secret
questions.text: The Secret `license` in namespace `payments` holds a key named `key`. Write its **decoded** value into `/opt/answers/license.txt` on the base host.
questions.solution:
kubectl -n payments get secret license -o jsonpath='{.data.key}' | base64 -d > /opt/answers/license.txt
    cat /opt/answers/license.txt

Secret data is base64-encoded, not encrypted; `base64 -d` reverses it. `kubectl get secret ... -o yaml` shows the encoded form.

checks.hint: /opt/answers/license.txt must contain the decoded license key

questions.title: Drain a node for maintenance
questions.text:
Node `cka2-node3` (the `pool=legacy` node) needs maintenance. Make it unschedulable and evict all workloads from it (DaemonSet pods may stay). Leave the node cordoned when you are done.

It is expected that the evicted `legacy` pods cannot be scheduled elsewhere afterwards.
questions.solution:
kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep cka2-node3
    kubectl drain cka2-node3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
    kubectl get nodes                        # cka2-node3 Ready,SchedulingDisabled
    kubectl get pods -A -o wide | grep cka2-node3   # only DaemonSet pods remain

`drain` cordons first, then evicts pods; their controllers recreate them elsewhere — here the `legacy` pods stay Pending because only this node tolerates their taint, which is fine for the task. If a node runs pods that no controller manages, `drain` refuses unless you add `--force` (which deletes them for good). `kubectl uncordon cka2-node3` would reopen the node afterwards; this task says to leave it cordoned.

checks.hint: cka2-node3 must be cordoned
workload pods are still running on cka2-node3

questions.title: API server down
questions.text:
`kubectl` commands against cluster `k8s-ops` fail with a connection error. The control plane node is `ops2-control`.

Find the cause and fix it so that `kubectl get nodes` works again against `k8s-ops`.
questions.solution:
kubectl config use-context k8s-ops
    kubectl get nodes                     # The connection to the server 10.0.1.21:6443 was refused
    ssh ops2-control
    sudo -i
    systemctl status kubelet              # running — so the static pod itself is the problem
    crictl ps -a | grep apiserver         # container keeps exiting
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml

One flag is misspelled: `--etcd-server=` must be `--etcd-servers=`. Fix it and save; the kubelet notices the manifest change and restarts the static pod within seconds. Then `exit` twice and re-run `kubectl get nodes`.

When the API server is down there is no `kubectl`: you work from the node with the manifest files under `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/`, the kubelet logs (`journalctl -u kubelet`), and `crictl`.

checks.hint: the kube-apiserver static pod manifest on ops2-control is still broken
the k8s-ops API server is still unreachable

questions.title: Kubelet will not start
questions.text: Node `ops2-node1` in cluster `k8s-ops` is `NotReady`. Starting the kubelet fails. Investigate on the node, fix the root cause, and bring the node back to `Ready` with the kubelet enabled.
questions.solution:
ssh ops2-node1
    sudo -i
    systemctl status kubelet                  # activating (auto-restart) / failed
    journalctl -u kubelet -n 20 --no-pager    # failed to load kubelet config file ... no kind "KubeletConfig" is registered
    vim /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml          # kind: KubeletConfig  ->  kind: KubeletConfiguration
    systemctl enable --now kubelet
    systemctl restart kubelet
    systemctl status kubelet                  # active (running)
    exit; exit
    kubectl get nodes                         # ops2-node1 Ready

The kubelet's own log is the fastest path to a broken-config diagnosis; typical culprits are `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`, the paths in `/etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-kubeadm.conf`, and certificates under `/var/lib/kubelet/pki`.

checks.name: kubelet
checks.hint: kubelet on ops2-node1 must be running and enabled
ops2-node1 is still NotReady

questions.title: Pods stuck in Pending
questions.text:
In cluster `k8s-ops`, the pods of Deployment `queue` in namespace `ops` are stuck in `Pending` and new pods never get scheduled anywhere.

Find the cause on the control plane node `ops2-control` and fix it so that all `queue` pods run. (Fix the API server first if you have not already.)
questions.solution:
kubectl -n ops describe pod <queue-pod>      # no events at all — nothing is scheduling
    kubectl -n kube-system get pods              # kube-scheduler-ops2-control in CrashLoopBackOff
    ssh ops2-control
    sudo -i
    vim /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml   # image tag is v1.31.0-broken -> v1.31.0
    exit; exit
    kubectl -n kube-system get pods              # scheduler Running
    kubectl -n ops get pods                      # queue pods Running

When every new pod stays Pending with no `Scheduled`/`FailedScheduling` event, suspect the scheduler itself rather than the pods.

checks.hint: the kube-scheduler static pod manifest on ops2-control is still broken

checks.name: queue
checks.hint: not all queue pods are running
